narrative:
Your application was denied because the prediction estimated an 80% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, the review treated that as a high risk and rejected your admission rather than accepting you with support or conditions.

The strongest factor by far was your third-year class standing. You are in the second decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile; this large gap strongly pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 35, below the accepted-student average of 37.18, although in this particular prediction it modestly leaned toward passing rather than failing. The third factor was your upper-middle family income bracket, which slightly increased the estimated risk of failure. Your first-year decile matched the accepted average, so it did not offset the third-year concern.

You should ask admissions for a human review and explain any circumstances behind your third-year grades. If feasible, retake the LSAT, strengthen your academic record, and seek pre-law advising; also consider applying to other schools or reapplying after showing improved preparation. Gender and race were not used in this decision.
